title: Ashenfall  -  The Bells Beneath the World

chapters.name: Prologue  -  The Last Wall
chapters.summary: Captain Aric sends the player beyond Stonehold after a Lantern Guard patrol disappears in Gloamwood. The sixth lantern is still burning somewhere beneath the roots.
chapters.player_question: Why did the patrol disappear, and why is one lantern still burning?
chapters.reveal: The ash is rising from below the forest, not falling from the sky.

chapters.name: Chapter I  -  Ashes of the Past
chapters.summary: Warden Kael and Keeper Havel reveal that the missing patrol was investigating a bell beneath Gloamwood. The player begins to understand that the forest is guarding something rather than merely being haunted.
chapters.player_question: Who rang the bell, and why does the forest protect it?
chapters.reveal: The sixth lantern was carried beneath the roots by the patrol itself.

chapters.name: Chapter II  -  The Bell Below
chapters.summary: The Sunken Catacombs expose the Hollow Saint and a bell that answers something older than the surviving kingdoms. The name Eir-Vhal enters the story.
chapters.player_question: What is Eir-Vhal, and why does the bell know the living?
chapters.reveal: Eir-Vhal was the site of the first great Veil stitching, and its seal is weakening.

chapters.name: Chapter III  -  A Door That Remembers
chapters.summary: The Black Road leads to a Citadel built around an ancient sealed door. Quartermaster Vey’s dead soldiers are returning, and the corruption is spreading outward.
chapters.player_question: What is behind the Door Below, and why does it remember people?
chapters.reveal: The threat is not simply escaping the Veil; it is learning the people who guard it.

chapters.name: Chapter IV  -  The Wastes Remember
chapters.summary: Briarfen reveals that the old road network is using living travelers, drowned lanterns and marked beasts as a memory chain. The trail then bends back into the Ashen Wastes.
chapters.player_question: Why are the old roads using living people to carry commands?
chapters.reveal: The road network is a memory channel, and the black seal is learning how to travel through it.

chapters.name: Chapter V  -  The Eastern Road
chapters.summary: The Sunscar caravans are being searched for names rather than supplies. Eastwatch becomes the first living outpost to receive commands from the dead court.
chapters.player_question: Who is sending royal orders through living roads?
chapters.reveal: The memory network uses travelers, ledgers and signal towers as a living communication system.

chapters.name: Chapter VI  -  The Crown Beneath
chapters.summary: Crownfall exposes the royal court behind the black seal. The Old Kingdom records reveal that the first stitching was a bargain involving memory and authority.
chapters.player_question: What did the old kingdom sacrifice to stitch the Veil?
chapters.reveal: The first stitching bound people, names and roads into the Veil so the world could forget what was beneath it.

chapters.name: Chapter VII  -  Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: The Veilscar Highlands reveal the network from above. Storms are not weather; they are pressure escaping through the memory roads.
chapters.player_question: Where do the memory roads converge?
chapters.reveal: They converge beneath the world and continue toward the drowned edge of the Hollow.

chapters.name: Chapter VIII  -  The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Nightveil Coast reveals that the memory court has routes beneath the sea. The drowned dead are preparing a final road toward the Hollow.
chapters.player_question: Who is speaking through the drowned court?
chapters.reveal: The Hollow is not simply a place; it is the surviving memory of an ancient court seeking a living voice.

chapters.name: Chapter IX  -  The First Stitch
chapters.summary: The player returns to the Black Citadel to trace the seal to its oldest surviving record and confront the thing that remembers names.
chapters.player_question: Who made the first stitch, and what did it cost?
chapters.reveal: The first stitch was made by people who chose to bind themselves into the Veil so the world could forget what they had seen.

chapters.name: Chapter X  -  The Bells Beneath the World
chapters.summary: The final road leads beneath the Old Kingdom. The bells are not calling the dead; they are calling the memories that were buried with them.
chapters.player_question: Can the Veil be repaired without becoming its next prisoner?
chapters.reveal: The player cannot simply close the door. They must decide which memories survive when the bells stop.

factions.name: Stonehold Council
factions.summary: Politicians who believe survival depends on controlling what the public is allowed to know.

factions.name: Lantern Guard
factions.summary: Soldiers who patrol the roads and keep the cities supplied, even when orders make less sense than the danger.

factions.name: Veil Wardens
factions.summary: Scholars and field agents who study Veil scars and fear that ignorance is becoming more dangerous than knowledge.

factions.name: Ashen Covenant
factions.summary: A scattered cult that believes the Veil is a prison and the things behind it deserve to be heard.

factions.name: The Hollow
factions.summary: Not yet understood as a faction. The name appears in old records for creatures, places, and perhaps something much larger.

characters.name: Captain Aric
characters.bio: A veteran who has buried three generations of recruits and refuses to call the current crisis a war. He believes discipline can hold back the dark, but privately fears the walls are already listening.
characters.motivation: Keep Stonehold alive without turning the Lantern Guard into the Council’s secret police.
characters.secret: He once received a report about Eir-Vhal and was ordered to destroy it.

characters.name: Warden Kael
characters.bio: A field warden who studies tears in the Veil. He distrusts the Council and suspects the violet ash is a message, not a disease.
characters.motivation: Understand the Veil before another generation is sacrificed to ignorance.
characters.secret: He believes the ash is communicating through repeated patterns, not spreading randomly.

characters.name: Keeper Havel
characters.bio: An old watcher who remembers the road before Stonehold was rebuilt. He knows a secret about the first Lantern Patrol that Aric never learned.
characters.motivation: Make sure the missing patrol is remembered as people, not a failed assignment.
characters.secret: He heard the sixth lantern answer the bell and has been afraid to tell Aric.

characters.name: Quartermaster Vey
characters.bio: A former soldier who survived the Citadel's fall. He wants the Citadel sealed, but needs adventurers strong enough to learn what is still moving inside.
characters.motivation: Keep the Citadel’s remaining soldiers from becoming another forgotten patrol.
characters.secret: His first squad disappeared beneath the Citadel years before the current crisis.

premise: Stonehold survives behind walls built over the scars of the Veil. Violet ash is rising from below, missing soldiers are returning as empty armor, and an ancient name - Eir-Vhal - is being spoken by things that should not know it. The player is not a chosen hero; they are one person whose decisions determine which truths survive.
themes: The cost of keeping the Veil closed
Ordinary people living beside ancient horrors
lore_principles: No prophecy makes the player important; their importance comes from what they choose to investigate and protect.
Major reveals should be foreshadowed by ordinary evidence: ledgers, patrol routes, tools, names, scars, and conflicting testimony.
NPCs should disagree about the truth instead of delivering identical exposition.
Side quests should reveal how the crisis changes real people, not only award combat rewards.
Every dungeon should answer one question while creating a more dangerous one.
